data.title: TypeScript
data.tagline: A language that checks written code for mismatched names and value types before it runs
data.learningOutcome: You can tell that a TypeScript error catches a mismatch before runtime, not whether a product rule is correct.
data.description: If you type `user.nmae` instead of `user.name`, TypeScript can flag it before the page runs when the object type is known. It checks declared code contracts; passing those checks does not prove the product logic is right.

learning.assumes: You have seen a name in code such as user.name.
learning.outcome: You can tell that a TypeScript error catches a mismatch before runtime, not whether a product rule is correct.

explanation.title: The same typo
explanation.text: The code asks for `nmae` when the declared property is `name`.

explanation.title: JavaScript finds out later
explanation.text: Without an extra check, the page may reach that line and get `undefined` at runtime.

explanation.title: TypeScript flags the contract
explanation.text: It compares the code to the types you wrote, usually in the editor, before the code is run.

data.boundary: Fix a type error first, but do not treat a clean type check as proof that pricing, permissions, or button flows meet the product rules.

lessonPractice.title: A user profile defines name as text, but code reads user.nmae, while a discount formula treats 20% as 20×. What can TypeScript solve?

options.label: Catch misspelled fields and type mismatches early, while business formulas still need tests
options.feedback: Types check data shape and usage, but cannot know whether a valid number carries the correct business meaning.

options.label: If there are no type errors, every field and discount result must be correct
options.feedback: Passing type checks does not prove logic; both 20 and 0.2 can be valid numbers.

options.label: Mark profiles and prices as any so the editor stops blocking execution
options.feedback: Any disables the structural checks needed here and delays spelling and usage failures.

data.agentPrompt: Define TypeScript types for profile and price data, remove misspelled fields and inconsistent shapes, and do not bypass them with any. After type checks pass, add discount-boundary tests because types cannot prove the formula.
